1.?

Rose surveyed 168 children in Arizona High School. She asked them about their favorite topics in math, between geometry and algebra. Her findings are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

Geometry Algebra Totals
Girls 28 63 91
Boys 56 21 77
Totals 84 84 168

Let B be the event that a randomly selected child is a "Boy" and G the event that a randomly selected child likes "Geometry". Estimate P(B∩G).

E
Thu, Jun 12th @ 4:03 PM|Elapsed: 0:39Correct

First, note that B∩G is the event that a randomly selected child is a boy and likes geometry.

To estimate the probability of B∩G, we

  • find the number at the intersection of the row "Boys" and the column "Geometry", and then

  • divide by the total number of data points in the table.

The number at the intersection of the row "Boys" and the column "Geometry" is highlighted in the table below.

Geometry Algebra Totals
Girls 28 63 91
Boys 56 21 77
Totals 84 84 168

Dividing by the total number of data points in the table (168), we get

P(B∩G)=56168=0.333.

To estimate the probability of I∪B, we

Flying Invisibility Other Totals
Female 16 18 12 46

School B has 300 students. Assuming the distribution of results is the same for both schools, estimate the number of School B students who are male and would choose to fly as their superpower.

Thu, Jun 12th @ 4:30 PM|Elapsed: 1:35Correct

To estimate the number of students who are male and would choose to fly as their superpower, we

  • find the number at the intersection of the row "Male" and the column "Flying", and then

  • divide by the total number of data points at the table.

The number at the intersection of the row "Male" and the column "Flying" is highlighted in the table below.

Flying Invisibility Other Totals
Female 16 18 12 46
Male 28 12 14 54
Totals 44 30 26 100

Dividing this number by the total number of data points in the table (100), we get

p=28100=0.28.

This represents the estimated probability that a randomly selected School A student is a male and chooses to fly as his superpower.

Finally, to find the estimated number of School B students who are male and would choose to fly as their superpower, we multiply the total number of School B students (300) by the probability above: n=300⋅p=300⋅0.28=84

  • add up the numbers in the row "6th grade" or the column "Beach", and then

  • divide by the total number of data points in the table.

Beach Countryside Totals
5th grade 55 30 85
6th grade 42 33 75
Totals 97 63 160

Adding up these numbers and then dividing by the total number of data points in the table (160), we get

p=55+42+33160=130160=0.81.

This represents the estimated probability that a randomly selected student is in 6th grade or likes to go to the beach on summer vacations.

Finally, to find the estimated number of students of John Adams Elementary School who are in 6th grade or like to go to the beach on summer vacations, we multiply the total number of students in the school (250) by the probability above: n=250⋅p=250⋅0.81=202.5=203,

rounded to the nearest integer.
